home.kicker: Identify Earth locations that analog the permanent Moon base locations and Mars
home.heroTitle: Where on Earth can we rehearse Mars?
home.heroText: Oman holds some of the planet's best exposures of rocks, salts and dunes that resemble what orbiters see on Mars. We compare five Omani sites with Mars landing regions, and one with the lunar south pole, using NASA data and an open, adjustable similarity index.
home.p1Text: Mars is the main target. The Moon is a secondary comparison, for terrain only and with a single region.
home.p2Text: All terrain is resampled to the same 463 m grid before comparing, because fine-resolution data always looks rougher.
home.p3Text: No Omani site is "just like Mars". Every card lists differences and data limits next to similarities, and each score carries a confidence value.
home.sitesSubtitle: Ranked by mean similarity to the Mars targets. Each card shows the best match and its breakdown by criterion.
home.rankTitle: Rank by mean similarity to Mars targets
home.validationText: Experts already chose the Dhofar desert for the AMADEE-18 Mars simulation (2018). Our index ranks it #{rank} of {total} Omani sites by mean similarity to Mars targets: a sign the method points in the right direction.

explorer.title: Explorer
explorer.intro: Pick an Omani site, then a target. The maps show both places side by side; the dashed box is the analysis window we clip from NASA data.

compare.title: Compare & adjust
compare.intro: Change the weight of each criterion and watch the score update. The same formula runs in Python for the published results.
compare.moonNote: Moon targets are compared on terrain only, so confidence is capped by data coverage.
compare.zeroWeights: All weights are zero: no score.

methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.intro: Python computes raw metrics once per site from NASA data and writes JSON. The website only reads that JSON, so there is no server or database. The similarity formula exists in both Python and TypeScript, and an automated test checks they give identical results.
methodology.normText: Each raw feature is mapped to 0–1 with a fixed range (values outside are clipped), so slopes in degrees and thermal inertia in TIU become comparable.
methodology.scoreText: For each criterion, the score is the mean of (1 − |difference|) over features available on both sides. The overall score is the weighted mean over criteria that have data.
methodology.confText: Confidence drops when data is missing (coverage) or when the two datasets have very different native resolutions (resolution match). Moon comparisons cover terrain only, so their confidence is lower by design.
methodology.scaleText: Comparing 30 m Earth DEMs with 463 m MOLA directly would be misleading. Every DEM is block-averaged to {scale} m before slope, roughness and relief are computed.
methodology.validationText: The Dhofar AMADEE-18 site was chosen by experts as a Mars analog. If our index ranks it highly against Mars targets, the method is working. Current rank: #{rank} of {total}.
limits: Terrain (NASADEM, MOLA, LOLA) and albedo (MODIS, TES) are computed from NASA data. Mineral indices (EMIT, CRISM) and thermal inertia are still provisional estimates and are marked as such on each site page.
Earth's atmosphere, water and gravity mean no site reproduces Mars or Moon conditions; we compare surface form and composition only.
Thermal inertia on Earth is estimated from apparent thermal inertia and needs local calibration.
Mineral indices are band-depth proxies, not quantitative abundances.
Weights are a judgement call. That is why the website lets you change them.

sources.title: Data sources
sources.intro: All datasets are open NASA (or partner) products. We clip a small window around each site instead of downloading full scenes.
sources.mapsText: Mars and Moon base maps: NASA Solar System Treks (Viking MDIM 2.1, MOLA, LRO WAC, LOLA). Earth: Esri World Imagery and OpenTopoMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors).
